statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke characterised the Chief Justice's remarks as a comparison of jobless young people with cockroaches and linked them to the movement's formation.
statements.assessment: The India Today interview records Dipke's own account. Its existence establishes what he said, not the full wording or context of the original judicial exchange.
statements.qualification: Attributable account; judicial context incomplete

statements.speaker: Rajeev Chandrasekhar
statements.statement: Chandrasekhar described the CJP phenomenon as showing signs of a cross-border influence operation.
statements.assessment: In the Indian Express interview, he expressly said he could not identify who mounted the supposed operation. No original funding, training, instructions or AEI correspondence is provided.
statements.qualification: Allegation; independent proof absent

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das described CJP's immediate plan as building a grassroots pressure movement, rather than joining electoral politics.
statements.assessment: NDTV published his statement on the day of the education minister's resignation. It is evidence of CJP's declared plan at that date, not proof of future conduct.
statements.qualification: Stated organisational intention

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Asked about his own political future, Ranka declined to rule out a later political career.
statements.assessment: NDTV's interview presents Ranka's answer alongside Das's organisational answer. They concern different questions; they do not establish a settled plan to contest elections.
statements.qualification: Attributed personal position

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said a negotiated agreement would cover withdrawal of FIRs against all protesters and organisers and prevent future FIRs.
statements.assessment: The Supreme Court's 1 September written order contains defined terms, scope and an exception concerning 2,873 persons. The interview did not itself constitute blanket legal immunity.
statements.qualification: Agreement claim; later order narrower

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said Pradhan's resignation had occurred before the CJP delegation arrived at the final government meeting.
statements.assessment: The Presidential communique establishes the resignation. The interview places the delegation's meeting after the decision, but does not prove why the minister resigned.
statements.qualification: First-person chronology; no sole-cause inference

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke described the movement as a response group working on education, unemployment and institutional trust, and said it would not join a political party.
statements.assessment: The Aaj Tak question-and-answer interview reports these positions. They should not be converted into a perpetual commitment or formal legal status.
statements.qualification: Stated intention; future actions unverified

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke denied that any political party created the protest movement and said supporters of multiple parties had attended.
statements.assessment: An interview records a denial of party direction. Documented former party links and public endorsements establish some associations, not who controlled organising or funding.
statements.qualification: Contested organisational account

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke estimated that 70–80% of attendees raised their hands when he asked whether they were first-time protesters.
statements.assessment: A self-reported show of hands is not a representative survey or count of all participants. No sampling method, event-by-event denominator or independent verification accompanies it.
statements.qualification: Unverified informal sample

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said ordinary citizens, doctors and professors donated food and refreshments for protesters.
statements.assessment: The statement identifies a claimed funding channel. It does not prove that all donations are accounted for or that competing funding allegations are true.
statements.qualification: Reported in-kind support; accounts not audited

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke argued that the amended examination-leak law focuses on penalties after leaks rather than on prevention.
statements.assessment: The interview documents a criticism of policy design. Whether the law contains sufficient preventive obligations requires clause-by-clause comparison with the enacted text and its rules.
statements.qualification: Policy interpretation; text comparison pending

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said he had demanded one crore rupees in compensation for each affected family and that payment had not been received by that interview.
statements.assessment: His statement concerns the position on 31 July. A later Supreme Court order directed a compensation framework within 90 days; this is not proof that money had been paid.
statements.qualification: Time-specific allegation; later order distinct

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said the movement would remain democratic and peaceful, while defending satire as a form of protest.
statements.assessment: A declared nonviolence principle is distinct from the behaviour of every individual during large demonstrations. Police and protesters dispute parts of the July clashes.
statements.qualification: Public commitment; conduct tested separately

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said the voter-roll revision had deleted about 13 crore names and cited it as the basis of the CJP protest.
statements.assessment: The public remarks used a broad count. Published totals combine distinct administrative categories; they do not by themselves quantify wrongful loss of voting rights by eligible citizens.
statements.qualification: Headline figure; interpretation needs reconciliation

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke described CJP as having no substantial cadre or resources, relying instead on public support.
statements.assessment: The claim establishes the founder's public presentation of the group, not audited assets or operating funds.
statements.qualification: Self-description; finances unaudited

statements.speaker: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Das said CJP was not competing with the Congress or AAP; Ranka said CJP had not reached out to Rahul Gandhi about the protest.
statements.assessment: The Indian Express directly attributes these answers. Not contacting one political leader is narrower than claiming no contacts with any party or activist network.
statements.qualification: Dated denial; broader ties not excluded

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke criticised train and Metro restrictions ahead of the protest and compared them with the Emergency period.
statements.assessment: The reported closures and orders need individual legal examination. Saying they were worse than a historical Emergency is an evaluative analogy, not an adjudicated fact.
statements.qualification: Documentable restrictions; historical analogy is opinion

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said CJP was independent of political parties, had not held specific discussions with Rahul Gandhi and shared some concerns with the INDIA bloc.
statements.assessment: The Indian Express and Loksatta recorded remarks to reporters. Shared public demands do not prove operational coordination, and a denial does not audit every relationship.
statements.qualification: Attributed account; formal ties not demonstrated

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke said CJP's roughly 25 million followers were not a vote bank belonging to a political party.
statements.assessment: A claimed audience metric does not measure verified membership, turnout or each follower's preferences. The claim should remain attributed to its speaker.
statements.qualification: Follower total and preferences not independently verified

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke argued that the two leaders were being held merely for raising the Indian flag at Jantar Mantar.
statements.assessment: Reuters reported police reliance on alleged breaches of undertakings and public-order restrictions. A five-day custody order is not a criminal conviction, but the flag alone is not the only reason given by police.
statements.qualification: Disputed characterisation of custody

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke asserted that the Supreme Court had minimised West Bengal voter deletions and helped the Election Commission in party-symbol disputes.
statements.assessment: The interview report notes that no case names were supplied for the party-symbol allegation. A judicial finding cannot be reconstructed safely from a speaker's paraphrase.
statements.qualification: Specific case attribution missing

statements.speaker: Rekha Gupta
statements.statement: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta called CJP an AAP 'B party' and questioned its choice of protest issues.
statements.assessment: The reported press conference presents Gupta's criticism. Earlier affiliations and parallel priorities do not alone establish formal subordination, funding or instructions.
statements.qualification: Political allegation; command chain not shown

statements.speaker: CJP representatives (speaker not named in clip summary)
statements.statement: CJP representatives appealed to lawyers to assist demonstrators facing detention or criminal complaints after the July protests.
statements.assessment: NDTV published a twenty-second press-conference clip with a description of the request. This establishes a call for legal aid, not the size or operation of any legal-support network.
statements.qualification: Documented public appeal; implementation unverified

statements.speaker: CJP representatives (speaker not named in clip summary)
statements.statement: CJP representatives said the government had agreed to withdraw protest-related FIRs and avoid fresh cases, and warned of renewed protests if this did not happen.
statements.assessment: NDTV dates the public warning to 27 July. The 1 September Supreme Court order later records defined relief and an explicit exception. Neither statement proves every police case was removed.
statements.qualification: Claimed negotiating terms; not a binding blanket exemption

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke announced an ultimatum calling for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation within 48 hours and further demonstrations if he did not resign.
statements.assessment: India Today reported the press conference and ultimatum. The ultimatum is a prospective mobilisation demand, not a legal determination or a verified outcome.
statements.qualification: Documented political demand; not proof of cause

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das demanded a pause on upcoming elections and criminal proceedings against the CEC and anyone allegedly directing him.
statements.assessment: India Today attributes these demands to Das. Criminal liability would require identifiable offences and evidence, and election postponement would require a lawful authority and basis.
statements.qualification: Political and legal demands; wrongdoing unproved

statements.speaker: Saurav Das / CJP delegation
statements.statement: The CJP press conference called for a return to 2025 electoral rolls, custody of SIR-related files under a Supreme Court-led committee, and repeal of the Election Commissioner appointments law.
statements.assessment: India Today reports these demands at the press event. Reverting an entire roll without testing additions, removals, deaths and relocations raises separate administrative and rights questions.
statements.qualification: Distinct reform proposals; effects unresolved

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke alleged that the CEC was acting on instructions from Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
statements.assessment: The accusation is attributable to Dipke's remarks to journalists. The recorded objections inside the ECI and the Commission's explanation are different evidence categories; neither establishes a ministerial instruction.
statements.qualification: Personal allegation; operational evidence absent

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke linked improved BJP vote shares in some states to the CEC's work, suggesting that an election official delivered gains unattainable in earlier periods.
statements.assessment: India Today reports his statement. Cross-state raw vote shares cannot determine why electoral outcomes changed, and no controlled comparison was supplied in the press report.
statements.qualification: Causal political accusation; numerical basis missing

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka alleged that some BJP-governed states intended to link welfare access to SIR voter-list inclusion.
statements.assessment: India Today directly attributes the assertion to Ranka. Electoral registration and welfare-scheme eligibility are separate legal systems; no specific state circular is reproduced in the report.
statements.qualification: Policy allegation; implementing notices not supplied

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das said conversations during the School Thik Karo campaign persuaded CJP to address electoral-roll concerns as a higher public priority.
statements.assessment: His account helps date the transition from education to election demands. Anecdotal conversations do not establish the prevalence or representativeness of that concern.
statements.qualification: Attributed account of programme evolution

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said CJP intended to march towards Jantar Mantar and sit wherever police halted participants, even if police withheld permission.
statements.assessment: The Indian Express interview documents an announced tactic before 10 October. An expressed intention does not prove what occurred on the day or establish whether particular acts were unlawful.
statements.qualification: Publicly stated civil-disobedience plan

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said any new lathi charge would lead CJP to demand Home Minister Amit Shah's resignation, and suggested police decisions required ministerial consent.
statements.assessment: The conditional demand is a documented position. Delhi Police's institutional oversight does not by itself demonstrate that a particular use-of-force order received the minister's prior instruction.
statements.qualification: Political warning; specific chain of orders unverified

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said elections were already being manipulated, the ECI was no longer independent and CJP would continue civil disobedience until its demands were met.
statements.assessment: The claim was reported in a direct interview. The ECI acknowledged some internal objections but described decisions as unanimous; internal procedural concerns alone do not establish manipulated votes.
statements.qualification: Contested systemic allegation; burden of proof remains

statements.speaker: Dhruv Rathee
statements.format: Public address at Bengaluru Freedom Park protest
statements.statement: Rathee told the Bengaluru protest audience he was not participating in a regime-change operation, while criticising election-commission transparency.
statements.assessment: The Indian Express attributes the statement to his public address at a CJP-associated gathering. His declared personal intention cannot prove or disprove every organiser's purpose, funding or external links.
statements.qualification: First-person denial of intent; independent organisational scope limited

statements.speaker: Prakash Raj
statements.format: Public address at Bengaluru Freedom Park protest
statements.statement: Prakash Raj alleged that the CEC acted under direction from Narendra Modi and Amit Shah and argued that SIR harmed civic rights.
statements.assessment: The Indian Express reports the allegation from Raj's public speech. Participation at a CJP event establishes open support on an issue, not formal CJP office or knowledge of a covert direction chain.
statements.qualification: Attributed protest allegation; no instruction trail shown

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka alleged that during the October 10 airport detention police separated CJP leaders and did not permit timely direct access to legal counsel.
statements.assessment: Hindustan Times published the interview, reporting his detailed account. The police account and any custody paperwork must be compared before findings about illegality or compliance.
statements.qualification: First-person account; official logs not reviewed

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka disputed police assertions that a peace bond prohibited CJP from organising another lawful demonstration.
statements.assessment: He described the form as a standard public-peace undertaking. Its effect depends on the signed instrument, the applicable statutory provision and court orders, not either side's characterisation in media.
statements.qualification: Legal interpretation disputed; bond text missing

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said an internal review involved CJP's core leadership and roughly 100 to 150 state coordinators and office-bearers.
statements.assessment: The number and meeting are attributed to a named speaker in an edited Q&A. The figure describes an alleged discussion, not verified national active membership.
statements.qualification: Self-reported internal attendance; no independent audit

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said CJP had no rift with opposition parties, despite its decision not to join their concurrent protest activity.
statements.assessment: Cooperation, shared slogans, participation and disagreement can coexist. A denial of a rift does not establish a coalition contract or an independent financing audit.
statements.qualification: Attributed relationship position; formal links separate

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Reported public appeal following press interaction
statements.statement: Dipke called for a 16 October gathering at Central Park, Connaught Place, with Indian flags to challenge the characterisation of flag-waving as an offence.
statements.assessment: Jansatta attributes the proposed time, venue and public argument to Dipke on 14 October. This records an announcement, not proof that a future gathering will happen or that an arrest was based on the flag alone.
statements.qualification: Prospective public call; event not yet observed

statements.speaker: Vijeta Dahiya
statements.statement: Dahiya said he was surprised when CJP organisers told him not to return to the July demonstration and subsequently removed his spokesperson role.
statements.assessment: His statement establishes how he described the phone call. Contemporaneous reporting confirms the office change and public controversy, but not every conversation or the organisers' private reasoning.
statements.qualification: Named first-person account; CJP disciplinary account separate

statements.speaker: Vijeta Dahiya
statements.statement: Dahiya said he had participated in the July 20 march before leaving temporarily, and rejected the suggestion that eating during the protest showed he abandoned the cause.
statements.assessment: The interview records his explanation. Viral videos from different locations or times cannot establish a continuous chronology of the march or individual conduct.
statements.qualification: Disputed sequence; edited clips insufficient

statements.speaker: Vijeta Dahiya
statements.statement: Dahiya said he remained aligned with the protest's objectives while acknowledging he was no longer a formal member or spokesperson.
statements.assessment: This distinguishes issue support from an actual organisational office. His continued public advocacy cannot be used to attribute later CJP leadership decisions to him.
statements.qualification: Dated self-description; position changed

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke alleged the 20 July police action happened at Amit Shah's behest and said the confrontation became a turning point in growing the movement.
statements.assessment: India Today's published exclusive records his characterisation. Protest growth and political motives need independent evidence; neither a minister's role nor a specific instruction can be inferred from office alone.
statements.qualification: Attributable allegation and political interpretation; no command record

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das described the CBSE chairperson and secretary transfers as inadequate to address underlying exam-system problems.
statements.assessment: The transfers and CJP criticism were reported. Whether the personnel changes addressed wider issues requires implementation and outcome evidence.
statements.qualification: Assessment of policy sufficiency; not a proven systemic failure

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das said the movement was willing to talk with government and opposition actors and invited participation without party banners.
statements.assessment: Willingness to meet multiple parties does not prove that any one party directed, financed or controlled CJP.
statements.qualification: Open invitation; no command relationship proved

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka rejected a political-party link, saying individual members' previous affiliations should not define the movement.
statements.assessment: A public denial is evidence of the speaker's position, not an independent test of control. Earlier affiliations alone also do not demonstrate current control.
statements.qualification: Attributed denial; independence not audited

statements.speaker: Vijeta Dahiya
statements.statement: Then-spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya said the movement reflected dissatisfaction among an entire young generation.
statements.assessment: The statement characterises a protest mood, not a representative estimate of the opinions of all young Indians. Dahiya later left the spokesperson role.
statements.qualification: Broad interpretation; representative data absent

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: On-stage public press interaction, Jantar Mantar
statements.statement: Responding to a reporter late on 20 July, Dipke said another march to Parliament would go ahead the following day.
statements.assessment: The report documents an intention at that time. A subsequent public announcement cancelled the proposed march after injuries. Neither statement by itself establishes a completed 21 July march.
statements.qualification: Dated intention; subsequently revised

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Public news conference after 20 July clashes
statements.statement: Dipke said CJP would stop further marches to Parliament to avoid more young people being injured.
statements.assessment: This narrows the previous evening's plan and applies to the Parliament march. It should not be misrepresented as a permanent commitment to end all public protest.
statements.qualification: Subsequent change of plan; not blanket end of protests

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Public news conference after 20 July clashes
statements.statement: Dipke said 150 protesters had been injured during the 20 July police action.
statements.assessment: Contemporaneous reports describe casualties, but published counts differ in coverage and whether police injuries are included. A precise protester-only total is not established here.
statements.qualification: Attributed injury count; scope unverified

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das announced CJP's plan to recruit members through its website.
statements.assessment: The conference establishes an intended recruitment channel, not a verified total of members, participants or chapters.
statements.qualification: Spoken organisational plan; enrolment not measured

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das said CJP was not raising funds at the time of the leadership announcement.
statements.assessment: The statement concerns claimed current fundraising practice. It cannot establish whether any money had previously been accepted or whether future funds were received.
statements.qualification: Attributable financing denial; independent records absent

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das said CJP would not presently transform into a conventional electoral political party.
statements.assessment: Creation of a leadership committee does not itself establish Election Commission recognition or registered-party status. The statement leaves later decisions open.
statements.qualification: Attributed organisational position; future status open

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.statement: Ranka said a CJP delegation planned to visit students protesting recruitment-exam irregularities in Jharkhand.
statements.assessment: The announced visit is evidence of public intention and possible issue coordination, not proof that the visit happened or that CJP organised the existing Jharkhand hunger strike.
statements.qualification: Announced trip; completion unverified

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: Das alleged that police seized CJP leaders' phones during airport detention without providing a formal seizure memo.
statements.assessment: The reported press remarks establish a specific allegation about police procedure, not a judicial finding of an unlawful seizure.
statements.qualification: Contested procedure allegation; documents missing

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: Das expressed concern that seized phones might have been hacked, cloned or used to plant material.
statements.assessment: The speaker framed phone tampering as a fear, not an observed forensic finding. No independent digital-forensic report is presented.
statements.qualification: Expressed suspicion; no device compromise demonstrated

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: Das alleged that more than 40,000 security personnel had been deployed in Delhi and described the area as a fortress.
statements.assessment: Published reporting documents extensive security restrictions, but varying figures and definitions prevent validating this specific deployment claim.
statements.qualification: Unverified personnel figure and evaluative language

statements.speaker: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: The two leaders accused right-wing groups of instigating attacks on protesters and alleged BJP support for those groups.
statements.assessment: Reports describe arrests of persons claiming a right-wing group association. That does not verify formal BJP involvement or the motives of all incidents.
statements.qualification: Attribution allegation; no demonstrated party instruction

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: Ranka characterised government actions as creating a war-like confrontation and said the political fight would continue.
statements.assessment: The remarks express a confrontational political interpretation. The existence of detentions and restrictions does not by itself mean that a constitutional Emergency was declared.
statements.qualification: Political characterisation, not a finding of war or Emergency

statements.speaker: Ashutosh Ranka
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India, Delhi
statements.statement: Ranka said supporters intended to hold another protest march that day and continue pressing for the election chief's resignation.
statements.assessment: A reported intention to march must not be counted as a completed method #38 without independent, dated occurrence evidence.
statements.qualification: Prospective action; execution separately verifiable

statements.speaker: Ajinkya Shinde
statements.statement: Shinde said the group would not be intimidated by the imprisonment of Das and Ranka and called for political change.
statements.assessment: Reuters identifies Shinde as speaking after he was released on bond. The message is not evidence that CJP uses any particular previously unobserved Gene Sharp method.
statements.qualification: Attributed political intention; no alleged command link

statements.speaker: Nitin Nabin
statements.statement: Nabin accused opposition groups and CJP-associated protesters of attempting to destabilise India at the behest of foreign forces.
statements.assessment: A recorded press-conference publisher summary establishes the political allegation, but identifies no foreign organisation, operative, transfer, AEI contact or instruction document. It does not prove CJP is controlled by AAP.
statements.qualification: Unsubstantiated allegation of outside direction

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India
statements.statement: Das alleged police entered Gurdwara Bangla Sahib with batons and weapons, removed sheltering protesters, and pressured staff not to assist them.
statements.assessment: The Tribune reports the allegation. Police and gurdwara representatives give distinct interpretations of the incident; an AAP-related complaint cannot automatically be attributed to CJP organisation.
statements.qualification: Disputed account; incident not independently resolved

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India
statements.statement: Das alleged a CJP Mumbai coordinator identified only as Pranay had been subjected to torture in custody.
statements.assessment: The report attributes this accusation to Das but provides no medical certificate, independent finding, complete identity, police account or judicial record. Publishing the attribution does not establish the alleged assault.
statements.qualification: Serious unverified allegation

statements.speaker: Ratna Singh
statements.format: Press conference, Press Club of India
statements.statement: Singh said police confined her vehicle for approximately nine hours and explained the restraint as orders from higher authorities.
statements.assessment: The News Minute explicitly identifies Singh as the speaker; a Tribune account seems to confuse her with Ranka in a passage using female pronouns. Duration, detention authority and legal justification need documentary corroboration.
statements.qualification: First-person detention account; procedural record absent

statements.speaker: Dhruv Rathee
statements.statement: Rathee publicly clarified that participating in the protest did not mean he was joining or formally affiliated with CJP.
statements.assessment: Economic Times presents a video item of the disavowal. Attending a demonstration or sharing a demand is distinct from holding party office; a denial also cannot by itself audit all private communications.
statements.qualification: Attributable denial; no contrary membership record

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke described the police video of his airport detention as edited and said requests to contact family and counsel after bereavement were denied.
statements.assessment: Indian Express reports Dipke's statement; police described the video as illustrating humanitarian assistance. The full original footage and call logs have not been reviewed.
statements.qualification: Contested account of edited footage

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Responding to remarks attributed to advocate Harish Salve, Dipke challenged critics of the movement to provide any foreign-direction evidence to authorities for investigation.
statements.assessment: Demanding evidence is an attributable public position. No independently verified AEI training, funding, operational direction or government exoneration follows from a challenge or denial.
statements.qualification: Challenge to accusers, not a financial clearance

statements.speaker: Mahua Moitra
statements.statement: Moitra supported the right of CJP-linked youth to demonstrate while saying senior opposition figures were keeping separate protest schedules and spaces.
statements.assessment: A televised interview summary records an account of distinct scheduling. Solidarity or common objectives do not prove financial sponsorship, membership, or CJP being directed by TMC or other opposition parties.
statements.qualification: Attributable political solidarity; no proven command chain

statements.speaker: Mahua Moitra
statements.statement: Moitra argued that accountability for the disputed electoral-roll exercise should extend beyond the CEC, calling for scrutiny of Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
statements.assessment: The interview attributes the political position to Moitra. It does not provide an authenticated instruction linking Shah to election-roll deletions or unlawful decisions.
statements.qualification: Political accountability argument, not proof of illegal instructions

statements.speaker: Ajay Alok
statements.statement: Alok defended restrictions on prohibited protest venues and accused opposition participants of fostering disorder by changing protest demands.
statements.assessment: The moderated debate documents a pro-restriction position. It does not resolve the legality or proportionality of the venue notification, arrest powers or any specific participant's conduct.
statements.qualification: Attributable public-order argument; legal merits disputed

statements.speaker: Randhir Jaiswal
statements.statement: When asked about alleged foreign financing of CJP-related protests, Jaiswal said he had no information on the matter to share at that time.
statements.assessment: The ministry later corrected viral posts falsely framing his answer as a declaration of no foreign funds. His public briefing neither confirmed allegations nor established their falsity.
statements.qualification: Official non-disclosure, not exoneration or confirmation

statements.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
statements.format: Public press conference before INDIA bloc march
statements.statement: Responding to a question about student and civil-society demonstrations, Gandhi described them and the INDIA bloc campaign against the Chief Election Commissioner as one protest.
statements.assessment: The press conference establishes a publicly voiced common cause. The Congress and CJP held separately organised actions, and Indian Express subsequently reported only an attempted Congress invitation through an intermediary, with CJP leaders unavailable. A common demand or offer of support cannot establish CJP governance or funding by Congress.
statements.qualification: Rhetorical unity, not proof of merged CJP command

statements.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
statements.format: Public press conference before INDIA bloc march
statements.statement: Gandhi alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had acted under pressure from Prime Minister Modi, Home Minister Shah and NSA Ajit Doval.
statements.assessment: The reporting establishes that Gandhi made the accusation, not that such directions were issued. Review of publicly authenticated Election Commission records, correspondence and any judicial findings is required before attributing illegal instructions to named officials.
statements.qualification: Serious political allegation; operational evidence not established

statements.speaker: Ajinkya Shinde
statements.format: Public reporter interaction with PTI video
statements.statement: Shinde asserted that his group only displayed the national flag and raised a patriotic slogan at Jantar Mantar, disputing the basis for custody.
statements.assessment: Independent coverage confirms a flag display, but police additionally alleged unauthorised entry through private premises, breached barricades, breach of peace bonds and disobedience of lawful directions. Allegations are not convictions, while the flag display alone does not describe every contested act.
statements.qualification: Contested factual characterization; police allege other acts

statements.speaker: Abhisht Hela (counsel for CJP leaders)
statements.format: Public statement to reporters after remand
statements.statement: Hela challenged the five-day custody order as lacking proper judicial application and objected to an executive police officer acting as Special Executive Magistrate.
statements.assessment: Hela's public criticisms frame issues to test against preventive-action law, the written remand order and any later judicial review. The procedural nature of the executive magistracy and the validity of this specific remand require documentary assessment; the counsel's position is not a judgment.
statements.qualification: Attributable legal criticism, not a court determination

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.statement: CJP's rapid growth reflects youth discontent; he interpreted government actions against CJP sites and accounts as fear of youth mobilisation.
statements.assessment: Reuters directly attributes and transcribes this assessment. It is Bhushan's interpretation of motive; the growth and alleged shutdown actions require independent records, and the motive cannot be independently confirmed.
statements.qualification: Assessment of motive, not established fact

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.statement: Bhushan said CJP would need carefully organised, calibrated street mobilisation rather than relying only on social media to deliver significant political change.
statements.assessment: A publicly recorded strategic recommendation is established. It does not establish that Bhushan directed or managed subsequent CJP events.
statements.qualification: Advice documented; operational role unproved

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.statement: Dipke acknowledged earlier AAP work but denied having an organisational or professional AAP relationship since his US studies or receiving formal party outreach at that time.
statements.assessment: Earlier AAP work is corroborated by later reporting and Bhagwant Mann's comments. His assertion of no current ties is an on-record denial, not a third-party governance audit. The denial referred to conditions as of the June interview, not October.
statements.qualification: Past association corroborated; current independence not independently audited

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.format: Reported public remarks at CPI office
statements.statement: Das publicly thanked AISF and SFI for helping organise and sustain CJP-linked protests.
statements.assessment: A news report reproduces a short excerpt and identifies the venue. It supports publicly acknowledged practical help, but the original complete footage, precise speech date and scope of work remain unauthenticated. The publisher's separate assertions of hidden control are not independently evidenced.
statements.qualification: Reported acknowledgment; full recording needed

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.statement: Bhushan argued that one consequence of CJP mobilisation was helping young people overcome fear of public protest.
statements.assessment: Indian Express attributes the statement to a Bengaluru talk. The social impact is his qualitative assessment, not a measured causal finding.
statements.qualification: Public evaluation, not quantitative proof

statements.speaker: Sanjeev Jha
statements.statement: AAP spokesperson Sanjeev Jha acknowledged historical AAP relationships among CJP organisers and maintained there was no recent contact.
statements.assessment: This is an attributable party spokesperson response. ThePrint also reports former AAP involvement across named CJP figures. 'No recent contact' is a party claim, not an independently audited communications history.
statements.qualification: Historical association admitted; recent-contact denial unverified

statements.speaker: Saurav Das
statements.statement: Das said youth and student organisations needed a united long-duration campaign and that changing the election commissioner alone would not meet broader electoral reform demands.
statements.assessment: PTI/IANS reporting establishes an on-record joint press conference with CJP, AISA, AISF, SFI and ASAP, the AAP student wing. A single public event proves announced shared protest goals, not a permanent joint governing body.
statements.qualification: Joint mobilisation documented; governance unproved

statements.speaker: Neha Bora
statements.statement: AISA president Neha Bora rejected political divisions among student organisations, opposition parties and civil society in the election-commission protest.
statements.assessment: Her unity statement is directly reported from the same joint briefing. It conveys a shared political position, not identity of organisations or centralised command.
statements.qualification: Shared campaign position, not merger

statements.speaker: Bhagwant Mann
statements.statement: Mann acknowledged that Dipke had worked in AAP's social-media team before leaving, while rejecting the claim that CJP was currently AAP's B team.
statements.assessment: The historical employment/volunteering link has converging on-record support from Dipke and Mann. Denial of present organisational control is not independently verified by transaction or communication audits.
statements.qualification: Past link corroborated; current control not established

statements.speaker: Arvind Kejriwal
statements.statement: Kejriwal said he planned to attend the 10 October CJP-called protest with his family and urged others to attend.
statements.assessment: His public invitation and intention to participate are attributed in the October 10 report; subsequent event presence, if asserted, must be checked separately. Political support does not imply that AAP operated CJP.
statements.qualification: Public political support documented; command unproved

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.statement: Yadav said the early October protests arose in parallel without an agreed phone-call sequence among student groups and opposition parties.
statements.assessment: The Federal publishes his own description of how the dates aligned. It is a participant-analyst account, not a verified review of all organisers' communications.
statements.qualification: Interview testimony; universal absence of prior coordination unproved

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.statement: Yadav advocated more deliberate coordination of protest activity while explicitly distinguishing this from a single banner or central command.
statements.assessment: An explicit public proposal for future synchronisation is documented. It is prospective and does not prove any previous instruction chain.
statements.qualification: Prospective proposal, not proof of established command

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.statement: Yadav described CJP, AAP, Congress, other parties, youth groups and unaffiliated citizens as separate strands of the anti-SIR mobilisation.
statements.assessment: This is his analytical taxonomy. It is compatible with several documented instances of joint activity while specifically not establishing a single controlling organisation.
statements.qualification: Distinct strands in interview; structure not independently audited

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.statement: Yadav estimated that many ordinary participants joined the protest outside formal party mobilisation and framed that as a strength.
statements.assessment: His estimates of fractions of non-affiliated attendance are subjective observations, not an audited participant survey. Public attendance should not be inferred from a rounded percentage.
statements.qualification: Observational estimate, not verified measurement

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.format: Speech at APCR public conference in Kolkata
statements.statement: Bhushan argued that officials responsible for unlawful cases, demolitions or other abuses should face legal accountability, not only action against isolated cases.
statements.assessment: Indian Express directly attributes the normative call to Bhushan at an APCR conference. The specific examples of wrongdoing he invoked are allegations to examine individually; an argument for punishment is not proof any named person committed a crime.
statements.qualification: Attributable public legal-advocacy statement, not findings of guilt

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.format: Speech at APCR public conference in Kolkata
statements.statement: Bhushan alleged that senior institutions were compromised by the ruling party and argued that public protest over electoral changes was necessary when institutions failed to act.
statements.assessment: Indian Express reports remarks about state institutions and police responses during October anti-CEC demonstrations. These are Bhushan's political and constitutional allegations, not an adjudicated finding about appointments, officials' motives or election manipulation.
statements.qualification: Attributable political allegations; underlying claims disputed or unproven

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Dipke described October 10 Metro and railway services as shut down in response to the protests.
statements.assessment: DMRC's sworn account says all 4,157 scheduled Metro trips ran, with entry/exit restrictions at 45 of 303 stations. Train operations and station access are different; the allegation of a complete Metro train shutdown is contradicted by the affidavit but the restrictions did occur.
statements.qualification: Contested overbroad transport characterisation

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Dipke argued that extensive security measures indicated the Prime Minister was protecting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
statements.assessment: The press conference confirms Dipke made the charge. Police restrictions and court proceedings are independently reported, but they do not by themselves establish why particular officials acted or an improper instruction from the Prime Minister.
statements.qualification: Political allegation; motive unproved

statements.speaker: Abhijeet Dipke
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Dipke maintained that unfurling the Indian national flag was not criminal and criticised the arrests of CJP leaders as unjustified.
statements.assessment: Flag display itself is not the same as trespass, breach of a bond, unlawful assembly or disobedience of a lawful order. The parties contest the surrounding conduct; detention and remand are not a final adjudication of guilt.
statements.qualification: Legality requires act-specific analysis

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Bhushan explicitly characterised the political mobilisation as aiming for regime change, with young people leading.
statements.assessment: The newspaper attributes a direct public conference statement to Bhushan. It is evidence of his expressed desired political outcome, not independently of his managerial authority, funding or legal wrongdoing.
statements.qualification: Express political objective; command chain unproved

statements.speaker: Prashant Bhushan
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Bhushan criticised the removal of Jantar Mantar's protest-site designation as restricting the right to dissent.
statements.assessment: His criticism is attributable. The authority, scope and legality of the denotification are separate legal questions; the High Court's separate 15 October Connaught Place order did not decide the entire Jantar Mantar dispute.
statements.qualification: Legal interpretation; merits not adjudicated here

statements.speaker: Neha Bora
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Bora described the electoral-roll protests as a cross-society struggle rather than the project of one organisation or political party.
statements.assessment: Her reported public remarks and the joint dais show open political collaboration across distinct named groups. The statement is not evidence of their formal merger or a single national command.
statements.qualification: Attributable coalition framing; no merger proved

statements.speaker: Neha Bora
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Bora alleged police detention, violence against journalists and seizure or obstruction of cameras during protests.
statements.assessment: Times of India attributes these remarks to Bora, but the report alone does not authenticate each asserted incident or identify which official allegedly committed it.
statements.qualification: Serious allegation; incident-level corroboration required

statements.speaker: Kapil Sibal
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Sibal warned that arbitrary mass changes or deletions from electoral rolls risk undermining electoral integrity.
statements.assessment: The warning is attributed to a public press conference. Its specific application depends on differentiating draft non-inclusion, final deletion, eligibility and available appeals. The warning does not establish a number of wrongly removed electors.
statements.qualification: Prospective legal warning; scale and illegality unresolved

statements.speaker: Prakash Raj
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Prakash Raj alleged misuse of Form 7 to seek removal of names from rolls, particularly of Muslim voters.
statements.assessment: The press account establishes that Raj made the allegation, not that targeting is proven. Form 7 objection applications, approvals, affected electors' eligibility and demographics require independent review.
statements.qualification: Allegation requiring disaggregated evidence

statements.speaker: Sheikh Salauddin
statements.format: Joint public press conference at the Press Club of India
statements.statement: Trade-union leader Sheikh Salauddin said his own name had been deleted from the electoral roll despite being an active voter.
statements.assessment: The reported oral statement is testimony of a claimed individual experience. It does not alone establish the legal status of a deletion or support a population-wide extrapolation.
statements.qualification: First-person account; record-level verification pending

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav said the October protests attracted young people outside established organisations and across previous party preferences.
statements.assessment: An edited interview records his interpretation of participation. It does not establish national participant proportions, the political preferences of attendees or CJP's membership composition.
statements.qualification: Interpretive observation; representativeness unverified

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav argued that SIR shifted a voter-registration burden onto people already on the rolls, contributing to exclusions when forms were not submitted.
statements.assessment: This describes a disputed effect of a revised administrative process. Different state circulars, stages, notification rules and avenues for restoration must be examined; omission at draft stage is not always permanent disenfranchisement.
statements.qualification: Procedural interpretation; audit required

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav estimated that approximately 130 million draft omissions might fall to around 115 million and compared expected register totals with adult-population estimates.
statements.assessment: These are his explicit projections and comparisons, not a verified final tally. Changes between draft and final rolls, eligible-citizen populations, migration, and denominator definitions must be reconciled.
statements.qualification: Estimate; final outcome unverified

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav alleged disproportionate targeted removal of Muslim voters in some states, particularly West Bengal.
statements.assessment: This serious allegation requires granular records distinguishing duplicate/deceased/moved electors, applications, notices, appeal outcomes and eligible voters. An election outcome or aggregate discrepancy does not establish intent.
statements.qualification: Targeting allegation; not established

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav recalled joining the Aam Aadmi Party after the anti-corruption movement and subsequently being expelled following internal disagreement.
statements.assessment: His account accords with contemporaneous reporting of the 2015 split. An earlier party position is not evidence of a current AAP-CJP instruction, funding or governing role.
statements.qualification: Prior affiliation; no current command demonstrated

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav described his participation in the 10 October march with Neha Bora and Prashant Bhushan, alleged police forcibly detained him and said students moved a barricade.
statements.assessment: A named participant gives first-person testimony. His own movements and arrest conditions can be checked, while the conduct he attributes to unnamed students cannot be assigned to CJP leadership or judged unlawful from this interview alone.
statements.qualification: First-person testimony; incident details require checking

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav asserted that BJP and Modi popularity had declined amid the protests while acknowledging that he lacked direct polling data to quantify the trend.
statements.assessment: The published Q&A expressly frames his view as impression-based. No statistically valid protest-causation or popularity change follows from anecdotal observation.
statements.qualification: Political assessment; no representative poll supplied

statements.speaker: Yogendra Yadav
statements.format: Edited telephone interview in The New Yorker
statements.statement: Yadav argued that protest energy should shape mainstream political organisations while retaining commitments to democratic political processes.
statements.assessment: This is a stated political prescription. It is not evidence of a completed merger, a secret committee, or a binding CJP-AAP-Congress-Left operational plan.
statements.qualification: Open advocacy; no operational chain shown

statements.speaker: Neha Bora
statements.format: Reported Press Club public press conference
statements.statement: Bora referred to the Bangladesh Gen Z mobilisation in discussing the Indian protests.
statements.assessment: The news feature says her comparison evoked the Bangladesh movement, which included violence. A comparison is not evidence of a public call to use violence, nor proof of a secret operational scheme. Exact words, intent and responses require the full unedited video.
statements.qualification: Context-dependent comparison; no violent instruction demonstrated

statements.speaker: Rajnath Singh
statements.statement: Singh accused Congress and political allies of using youth demonstrations to create confrontation and disorder rather than constructive political activity.
statements.assessment: The accusation is attributable to an identified government minister at a recorded public press conference. Public coalition appearances do not independently establish a covert coordinated campaign, unlawful actions by the entire movement or a unified command.
statements.qualification: Political accusation; central coordination unproven

statements.speaker: Rajnath Singh
statements.statement: Singh said some actors drew inspiration from Bangladesh to bring down India's government and framed opposition mobilisation as a plot to acquire power through instability.
statements.assessment: The record documents his interpretation of opponents' words, not an established foreign sponsor, an operational conspiracy or an intent to employ violence. Any comparison with Bangladesh or Gene Sharp is insufficient by itself to prove foreign direction.
statements.qualification: Allegation of destabilisation; evidence of operational plot absent

statements.speaker: Rajnath Singh
statements.statement: Singh asserted that the opposition's protest was not genuinely about electoral-roll reform or the Chief Election Commissioner but about changing political power.
statements.assessment: Participants have openly advanced electoral-roll and political demands in overlapping events. Their sincerity or private motivations cannot be inferred solely from a minister's assertion; distinct organisations and platforms must be separated.
statements.qualification: Political motive attribution; not empirically proved

statements.speaker: Pawan Khera
statements.format: Public on-camera media interaction with ANI
statements.statement: Khera defended the opposition's aim of changing the government and expressly described electoral victory as the democratic mechanism for regime change.
statements.assessment: An explicit commitment to pursuing change through elections is attributable to Congress's speaker. It does not establish that CJP adopted a formal Congress election campaign or that other speakers share precisely the same aims.
statements.qualification: Public electoral position; no shared CJP command proved

statements.speaker: Pawan Khera
statements.format: Public on-camera media interaction with ANI
statements.statement: Khera argued that BJP politicians had supported Prashant Bhushan's earlier anti-government protest work around 2012–2013 and were inconsistent in criticising him now.
statements.assessment: This is a political interpretation about historical support. It should be checked against dated BJP statements and the earlier movement's leadership roles. Past endorsement by any party is not evidence of current CJP sponsorship.
statements.qualification: Historically testable criticism; current organisational link not shown

statements.speaker: Udit (Delhi protest participant; first name published)
statements.format: On-site interview with Indian Express reporters, Palika Bazaar
statements.statement: An attendee carrying a tricolour questioned restrictions on flag display and said heavy police deployment prompted him to attend.
statements.assessment: The reporter observed an individual with a flag and recorded his opinion. The quotation does not establish that every location-specific order targeted flags alone or that restrictions have been judicially ruled unlawful.
statements.qualification: Participant opinion; legal restrictions need separate testing

statements.speaker: Shivam (Delhi protest participant; first name published)
statements.format: On-site interview with Indian Express reporters, Connaught Place
statements.statement: An attendee said he came after social-video exposure, considered himself independent of parties and regarded CJP as a social-media-driven youth mobilisation.
statements.assessment: This is one participant's narrated reason for attending. It provides a valid counterexample to automatic party-membership attribution, not a representative breakdown of all attendees or a tested claim about social media influence.
statements.qualification: First-person attendance explanation; not a representative survey

statements.speaker: Sonu Yadav (Delhi protest participant)
statements.format: On-site interview with Indian Express reporters, Palika Bazaar
statements.statement: An attendee reported being detained twice in the preceding three days and said he concealed his flag en route to the demonstration to avoid detention.
statements.assessment: The published interview establishes first-person testimony, not the legal basis or precise timeline of the alleged earlier detentions. Neither the attendee's actions nor reported police conduct can be attributed to CJP organisers without evidence.
statements.qualification: First-person testimony; detention history unverified

statements.speaker: Advocate Anandini Fernandes (Mumbai protest participant)
statements.format: On-site interview with Jansatta reporters, Azad Maidan
statements.statement: A Mumbai participant said she reached the permitted protest without seeing reliable official CJP mobilisation information and criticised the lack of organiser coordination.
statements.assessment: This is participant testimony about the Mumbai event, corroborated in part by the reporter's observation of a small gathering. It rebuts a sweeping claim of seamless nationwide logistics but is not a governance audit.
statements.qualification: Participant criticism; wider operational structure unverified

statements.speaker: Pramodita (Mumbai protest participant; first name published)
statements.format: On-site interview with Jansatta reporters, Azad Maidan
statements.statement: A student participant said fear of detention and inadequate communication may have contributed to low Mumbai attendance.
statements.assessment: This is an explicitly conditional personal assessment. It does not quantify a causal contribution of police deterrence versus late notification or organiser logistics. It is consistent with a reporter-observed small turnout.
statements.qualification: Unquantified causal assessment; coordination gaps reported

statements.displayDate: 15 October 2026 (New York local date; reported 16 October)
statements.speaker: Salman Rushdie
statements.format: Public spoken remarks at Asian American Writers' Workshop fundraising dinner
statements.statement: Rushdie praised the Indian youth protesters and offered symbolic public support to the CJP cause at a New York literary fundraising event.
statements.assessment: News outlets attribute public remarks to Rushdie via journalist Amitava Kumar's on-site account. The fundraising event was for the Asian American Writers' Workshop, not documented as a CJP fundraiser. Praise is not evidence of remittances, AEI sponsorship or operational instruction.
statements.qualification: Reported public solidarity; no CJP foreign financing shown

statements.displayDate: 15 October 2026 (New York local date; reported 16 October)
statements.speaker: Mira Nair
statements.format: Reported public remarks at Asian American Writers' Workshop fundraising dinner
statements.statement: Nair expressed pride in young Indian demonstrators defending democracy and publicly associated herself with the protesters in symbolic language.
statements.assessment: The on-site account describes personal public endorsement, not a CJP office, finance arrangement or transfer. Her public political opinion and the dinner's literary fundraising purpose must not be conflated with sponsorship of CJP.
statements.qualification: Reported artistic solidarity; no formal role or funding evidenced
